root.name: Ruy Lopez: Steinitz Defense Deferred, Lipnitsky Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O d6 6. Bxc6+ bxc6 7. d4 Bg4

overview: White has traded Bxc6 and played d4, and Black’s doubled c-pawns give the bishop pair and the e4 pressure. The most played branch is the Boleslavsky 7...Nxe4 8.Re1 f5 9.dxe5 d5, where Black holds e4 with ...f5 and the knight. The Lipnitsky 7...Bg4 pins the knight instead.

white_ideas.idea: Exploit the doubled c-pawns by pressing e5 and e4 with Re1 and Nc3
Seek an endgame with a better structure

black_ideas.idea: Hold e4 with ...f5 and ...d5, using the bishop pair
Seek piece activity on the open lines

typical_structures.structure: Black doubled c-pawns, open centre with e5 exchanged

character.notes: The Boleslavsky line is forcing and tactical. Tactical.

gambit.notes: Pawns are won back through Re1 or dxe5.

level.notes: Needs some forcing lines and understanding.

sublines_that_differ.name: Lipnitsky Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: A quieter pin than the Boleslavsky 7...Nxe4.
